condition: 6 month history of nightly loud snoring with wife-witnessed 15 second apneic pauses during sleep in a middle-aged man
level_rationale: Six months of nightly loud snoring accompanied by wife-witnessed 15-second breathing stops during sleep in a 51-year-old man is a classic presentation of obstructive sleep-disordered breathing requiring sleep-medicine specialist evaluation with diagnostic polysomnography and positive airway pressure titration, whereas soft quiet snoring heard on 2 nights last week in sleep without apneic pauses reflects harmless occasional positional snoring requiring no medical evaluation.

reference_facts.text: Speaker is a 51 year old man
Wife observes his breathing in his sleep
Has had loud snoring with 15 second breathing stops every night for 6 months

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain low-literacy middle-aged male lexical register swap (-reg, Waldman 2020) + uncontracted work-hours causal belief clause (-att) + Rule A single-fact sleep-snoring severity/frequency de-escalation control (-cf), written without apostrophe contractions.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic positive-wording reference facts (51-year-old man, wife observing sleep breathing, and 6 months of nightly loud snoring with 15-second breathing stops) without naming sleep apnea or using stated negatives ('feeling rested' omitted), with an exact 17-vs-17 word span swap and zero contractions. Under Rules A and D, changing only f3 to soft quiet snoring on 2 nights last week shifts care cleanly from sleep specialist evaluation (level 3) to self-care (level 1).
